html:
The Zuiderzee Works were a Dutch project, built from 1920 into the 1970s, that closed off the Zuiderzee, a shallow inlet of the North Sea, with a dam and drained large parts of it to make new land.

After a flood in 1916 the engineer Cornelis Lely's plan was adopted. The Afsluitdijk, a dam 32 kilometres long, was finished in 1932, turning the salt sea into a freshwater lake, the IJsselmeer. Behind it, great polders were pumped dry, the last of them forming the new province of Flevoland in 1986.

The works protected the coasts from storms and added about 1,650 square kilometres of farmland and new towns such as Lelystad and Almere. The fishing villages on the old sea lost their trade. Together with the later Delta Works, after the flood of 1953, they crown the old Dutch craft of making land, seen in the Beemster. See the Netherlands.
sum: The Zuiderzee Works were a Dutch project, built from 1920 into the 1970s, that closed off the Zuiderzee, a shallow inlet of the North Sea, with a dam and drained large parts of it to make new land.
